quotes.text: Songwriting is still the same uncomplicated process it was when I was 12 years old writing songs in my room
There are definitely moments when it's like this cloud of an idea comes and just lands in front of your face, and you reach up and grab it.

A lot of songwriting is things you learn, like structure, cultivating that skill and knowing how to craft a song. But there are mystical, magical moments—inexplicable moments—when an idea that is fully formed just pops into your head.
To me, Tom Petty represented a kind of songwriting I idolized: complex simplicity.
It said so much in the lyrics, the concepts, the stories, the message, the nuances … but always b
The ideas are my favorite part of everything I do. That moment where you're like, 'Oh, I know what it's called,' or 'I know what the hook is now.'

I remember when I used to get an idea when I was 12 years old in my room. I used to get an idea and I'd be like, 'Yes, idea!' And then I'd get this fear and almost sorrow that no one was ever going to hear it. 'I'm never going to get to make this into something. It's just mine.'
There's something cute about that … but I want to make something.

Fans are my favorite thing in the world. I've never been the type of artist who has a line drawn between their friends and their fans… I'll hang out with them after the show. I'll hang with them before the show.
For me, genres are a way for people to easily categorize music. But it doesn't have to define you. It doesn't have to limit you.
